participantInstructions: This event will be presented through the reading of the 21st Century Skills, the Performance Indicators, and the Case Study Situation on the following pages. You will have up to thirty (30) minutes to prepare your presentation. You will have up to fifteen (15) minutes to make your presentation to the judge and to answer the judge's questions. Both team members must participate in the presentation and in answering the judge's questions. You will be evaluated on how well each performance indicator is met. Turn in all of your notes and prepared materials to the judge at the conclusion of the presentation.
situation:
You are the accounts manager and the sales operations manager at VANTAGE RX PARTNERS, a contract sales organization that supplies trained pharmaceutical sales representatives to small drug manufacturers that cannot yet afford an in-house sales force. The owner (judge) of Vantage Rx Partners has called this meeting because a decision must be made before the end of the week, and the owner (judge) wants your recommendation before responding to the client.

Vantage Rx Partners is two years old and still operating on its first round of seed funding, which is nearly spent. Its only active contract is with COREVIA BIOSCIENCES, a manufacturer preparing to launch a new cardiology drug. Under that contract, Vantage assembled and trained a twelve-person field team over four months, and Corevia agreed to pay Vantage a fixed monthly fee for each representative for the full twelve-month term, regardless of how quickly the drug is adopted by physicians.

Ten days before launch, Corevia's vice president of sales asked to amend that payment term. Corevia wants to replace the fixed monthly fee with a commission paid only on prescriptions the drug actually generates, citing uncertainty over how fast physicians will switch from existing treatments. Corevia's request would lower Vantage's guaranteed income during the slow early months of a new drug launch, months the field team was told to expect steady pay for, and several representatives had already turned down other offers to join Vantage for this contract.

Vantage has no other signed contract to replace Corevia's revenue if the relationship ends, and Corevia has hinted it could take its business to a competing contract sales organization if Vantage will not accommodate the change. Refusing the amendment protects the field team's expected pay but risks the company's largest and only account at a time when Vantage's funding will not stretch through a second launch delay or a lost client.

Agreeing to the amendment keeps Corevia as a client and preserves the revenue Vantage needs to reach its next funding milestone, but it shifts the financial risk of a slow launch onto representatives who were hired and trained under a different promise. The owner (judge) wants you to weigh what Vantage owes its client against what it owes the team it recruited, and to recommend whether to accept Corevia's new term, hold the original term, or propose a different arrangement.

The owner (judge) will greet you at the start of the meeting, ask you to present your recommendation, and listen carefully to your reasoning before deciding how to respond to Corevia. The owner (judge) may ask follow-up questions about the reasoning behind your recommendation during the presentation. At the close of your presentation, after any questions have been answered, the owner (judge) will thank you for your work and close the meeting.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the owner (judge) of Vantage Rx Partners. Business background is the same as the situation above. Corevia Biosciences has asked to change a payment term in your contract with them just before its drug launches, and your accounts manager and sales operations manager have asked to meet with you before you respond to the client. You want to hear whether they recommend accepting Corevia's new term, holding the original term, or proposing a different arrangement, and you want to understand the reasoning behind whatever they recommend.

You will greet the participants and ask them to share their ideas. You may ask the following:
judgeQuestions: Why might Corevia want to change this payment term now, so close to launch?
Who is affected most if Vantage agrees to the change, and why does that matter to the company?
